business_model.claim: Harley-Davidson operates three reportable segments: Harley-Davidson Motor Company (HDMC), LiveWire, and Harley-Davidson Financial Services (HDFS).
quotes: The Company has three reportable segments: Harley-Davidson Motor Company (HDMC), LiveWire, and Harley-Davidson Financial Services (HDFS).

business_model.claim: HDMC designs, manufactures and sells Harley-Davidson motorcycles, motorcycle parts, accessories, apparel, and licensed trademarks to retail customers primarily through a global network of independent dealers.
quotes: HDMC designs, manufactures and sells Harley-Davidson motorcycles. HDMC also sells motorcycle parts, accessories, and apparel as well as licenses its trademarks.
HDMC's products are sold to retail customers primarily through a network of independent dealers.

business_model.basis: stated in P1 (10-K Item 1 Business), table heading 'as a percent of total revenue'

Licensing | 0.6 | 0.6 | 0.6
Other products and services | 1.9 | 1.7 | 1.6

business_model.claim: LiveWire is an all-electric motorcycle brand that sells electric motorcycles, electric balance bikes, electric bikes, parts, accessories, and apparel in the United States and certain international markets.
quotes: LiveWire is an all-electric motorcycle brand with a focus on pioneering the two-wheel electric motorcycle space. LiveWire sells electric motorcycles, electric balance bikes for kids, electric bikes, parts and accessories and apparel in the United States and certain international markets.

business_model.basis: stated in P3 (10-K Item 7 MD&A, HDFS Transaction section)
business_model.claim: HDFS earns revenue from interest on retail finance receivables and, following the 2025 HDFS Transaction, from loan servicing fees at 1% per annum for prime loans and 2.5% per annum for subprime loans.
quotes: HDFS earns loan servicing fees over the period it services loans purchased by the counterparties at a rate of 1% per annum for prime loans and 2.5% per annum for subprime loans.

business_model.basis: stated in P3 (10-K Item 7 MD&A, HDFS Transaction section)
business_model.claim: In the second half of 2025, HDFS sold $4.1 billion of retail finance receivables, deconsolidated $1.9 billion of net finance receivables and $1.7 billion of related debt, and two counterparties acquired 9.8% of HDFS equity for a combined $46.6 million.
quotes: HDFS sold $4.1 billion of retail finance receivables originated prior to the HDFS transaction, resulting in the release of the related allowance for credit losses and contributing to a $191.4 million benefit in the provision for credit losses in 2025.
Each of the counterparties paid $23.3 million cash to acquire 4.9% of HDFS based on a multiple of approximately 1.75x HDFS's post-transaction equity carrying value for a total of 9.8% of HDFS.

business_model.basis: stated in P5 (10-Q MD&A Outlook) and P7 (8-K Q3 earnings release)
business_model.claim: HDMC revenue is driven primarily by wholesale motorcycle shipment volume, which the Company aligns to worldwide dealer retail sales to manage dealer inventory health.
quotes: Based on the results of the first half of 2026, the Company now expects both 2026 wholesale shipments and worldwide dealer retail sales of Harley-Davidson motorcycles of 133,500 to 138,500, which is an increase from the Company's previous expectation of 130,000 to 135,000 units.
HDMC revenue of $964 million in the quarter, was down 10 percent vs. prior year driven by lower shipment volume.

business_model.basis: stated in P3 (10-K Item 7 MD&A Overview)
business_model.claim: Worldwide dealer retail unit sales of new Harley-Davidson motorcycles decreased 12.4% in 2025 compared to 2024, driven by high interest rates and depressed consumer sentiment affecting premium discretionary spending.
quotes: Worldwide dealer retail unit sales of new Harley-Davidson motorcycles decreased 12.4% in 2025 compared to 2024.

During 2025, a challenging economic environment, including high-interest rates and depressed consumer sentiment resulting from economic uncertainty, continued to adversely impact consumer demand for premium discretionary products, including the Company's motorcycles.

business_model.basis: stated in P3 (10-K MD&A) and P5 (10-Q MD&A Outlook)
business_model.claim: HDMC operating results are sensitive to manufacturing leverage: lower production volumes spread fixed costs over fewer units, raising per-unit cost and compressing margins.
quotes: Operating income was also unfavorably impacted by unfavorable manufacturing leverage related to higher fixed costs per unit on lower production and shipment volumes as well as the impact from new or increased tariffs implemented in 2025, partially offset by favorable changes in pricing, shipment mix, foreign currency rates and raw material costs.

The Company continues to expect a reduced level of production in 2026 to negatively impact HDMC's full year operating margins due to unfavorable manufacturing leverage as fixed costs are allocated over fewer units produced resulting in a higher unit cost.

business_model.basis: stated in P3 (10-K MD&A, tariff table) and P5 (10-Q MD&A, tariff estimate)
business_model.claim: New or increased U.S. tariffs implemented in 2025 cost the Company approximately $67 million in 2025, and the Company estimated full-year 2026 tariff costs of $75 million to $105 million as of February 2026, later narrowing to $75 million to $90 million as of July 2026.
quotes: During 2025, the total cost of new or increased tariffs implemented in 2025 that the Company incurred was approximately $67 million(a).

The Company's estimate of the cost of these tariffs for the full year 2026(1) as of July 17, 2026 ranges from $75 million to $90 million, which is consistent with the Company's previous estimated range.

business_model.basis: stated in P5 (10-Q MD&A, Back to the Bricks section)
business_model.claim: Under the Back to the Bricks strategic plan announced in Q2 2026, the Company targets at least $150 million in cost reductions compared to the 2025 cost base plus an additional $75 million benefit to HDMC profitability, for a total annual benefit of at least $225 million, to be fully realized by end of 2027.
quotes: The Company expects these cost reduction actions to reduce its costs by at least $150 million compared to its 2025 cost base.

In addition to these savings, the Company has set a target to achieve at least an additional $75 million benefit to HDMC profitability during the same time period through improved cost leverage and other activities that would result in a total annual benefit of at least $225 million.

business_model.basis: stated in P1 (10-K Item 1 Business), segment revenue table in thousands
business_model.claim: In 2025, total consolidated revenue was $4,473,175 thousand, comprising HDMC $3,578,308 thousand, LiveWire $25,671 thousand, and HDFS $869,196 thousand.

business_model.basis: stated in P3 (10-K MD&A, Interest Rates and HDFS Transaction sections)
business_model.claim: Higher interest rates adversely impact both HDFS's interest income margin (higher cost of funds) and consumer demand for financed motorcycle purchases, while the HDFS Transaction structurally reduced HDFS's interest income going forward.
quotes: The current higher interest rate environment has adversely impacted HDFS' interest income margin due to a higher cost of funds that is only partially offset by increased interest rates on financing products sold by HDFS.

As a result, the Company expects HDFS's operating income will be reduced as it earns less interest income on HDFS's lower retail finance receivable balance, partially offset by new retail loan servicing fees for servicing loans that have been sold and from expected ongoing sales of loans under the Forward Flow Agreement(1).

business_model.basis: stated in P1 (10-K Item 1, Raw Materials) and P2 (10-K Item 1A, Risk Factors)
business_model.claim: HDMC's principal raw materials include steel and aluminum castings, forgings, steel sheet and bar, and purchased components such as fuel injection systems, batteries, tires, seats, and electrical components, with supply chain disruptions and inflation as key cost risks.
quotes: HDMC's principal raw materials include steel and aluminum castings, forgings, steel sheet and bar. HDMC also purchases certain motorcycle components including, but not limited to, electronic fuel injection systems, batteries, tires, seats, electrical components, instruments and wheels.

Inflationary pressures, including on manufacturing, and the availability of components and raw materials, such as rare earth elements, or instability in logistics, including the escalating tensions between the U.S. and foreign leaders regarding the Panama Canal, and related costs may negatively impact the Company's profitability.
